howDoI.q: How do I make a torch flame that flickers?
How do I stop a row of torches flickering in step?
How do I make a flag wave on a pole?
How do I make a waterfall that falls?
How do I make a waterfall wider than one block?
How do I make sparks that rise from a fire?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Flicker and Flow is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. This one is about things that move in place: a torch's flame, a flag in the wind, a waterfall, a fire and its sparks. It has three short levels, a castle hall, a cliff and a hilltop at night. Each takes a minute or two.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

The Left and Right arrows walk and Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Nothing in this game can hurt you. For a sea that moves the same way, see Waves on the Shore; for stars that blink out of step, see Twinkle, Twinkle.

pages.head: Level 1: The Torch Hall
pages.html:
Level 1: The Torch Hall

A castle hall with a brick floor and dim stone walls. EVEN TIMES MAKE A PULSE stands by two torches whose flames grow and shrink in a steady beat. UNEVEN TIMES MAKE IT FLICKER stands by four torches that flicker, and TWO LOOPS KEEP TORCHES APART after them. A WAVE MOVES ALONG TWO BLOCKS stands by two flags on poles near the door.

There is nothing to collect. Stop by each torch and watch it for a moment.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A flame is a loop. Open hall.bbl in the blocks editor and pick pulse.0. Its Next block is pulse.1 and its Time is 5 ticks (there are 18.2 ticks in a second). pulse.1 turns into pulse.2, then pulse.3, and pulse.3 turns back into pulse.0. The flame grows and shrinks and every frame lasts the same time, so it pulses like a lamp.
  • A flicker is a loop with uneven times. The torches by the second sign use flameA.0 to flameA.3. Their frames do not grow and shrink in order: the flame leans left, shrinks, stands tall, then leans right, and the times are 3, 5, 2 and 4 ticks. The eye cannot find a beat, so it reads as a fire.
  • Two loops keep torches apart. The game keeps one clock for each block number, so every torch drawn with flameA flickers at the same instant. A hall of them would flicker in step. The torches here alternate flameA with flameB, a second loop with its own frames and times (4, 2, 6 and 3), and the two are at the same frame only about a fifth of the time.
  • The torch's holder. Under each flame block is sconce, the stick, its iron ring and the bracket, which never changes. A torch is two blocks, a flame that moves above a holder that does not.
  • A flag is a wave moved along its cloth. The flag is two blocks side by side, flagA (the pole and the first half of the cloth) and flagB (the rest and the swallow tail). Each is a loop of four frames in which the wave sits a quarter of its length further along, and both take 6 ticks a frame, so they step together and the wave runs across the join. A steady wave wants even times. Above the cloth are pole.top, a pole with a gold ball, and below it pole.mid, twice.

pages.head: Level 2: The Falls
pages.html:
Level 2: The Falls

A cliff on a green meadow, with a waterfall four blocks wide falling into a shallow pool. STREAKS SLIDE DOWN 5 PIXELS A FRAME stands at the start. THE TOP AND FOOT ARE LOOPS TOO and FOUR BLOCKS MAKE A WIDE FALL stand past the cliff, before the door.

Walk in front of the fall and through the foam at its foot. Nothing here is wet enough to hurt.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The body is a pattern that slides. Open falls.bbl and pick fallM.0. It is a pale blue block with white and blue streaks. fallM.1 is the same picture with every streak moved down 5 pixels, fallM.2 moved 10 and fallM.3 15; a streak that leaves the bottom comes back in at the top. A block is 20 pixels high, so four frames of 5 pixels make one whole turn of the pattern and fallM.3 turns back into fallM.0 with no jump. The same pattern in the block above and the block below joins without a seam. Every frame lasts 3 ticks: even times, because falling water has no beat.
  • Four blocks make a wide fall. A block is only 20 pixels, so a wide fall is blocks side by side: fallL, fallM, fallN and fallR, each with its own streaks, so the whole does not repeat across its width. The left and right ones are shaded where the water meets the rock. All four take 3 ticks a frame, so they step together.
  • The lip is a loop of its own. At the top, lipL to lipR show a surface that curls over the edge, with ripples sliding sideways, and under it the body's own streaks, in the same columns and sliding the same 5 pixels. Its frames last 3 ticks, like the body's, so a streak runs on from the lip into the body without a jump.
  • The splash keeps the body's beat. At the foot, splashL to splashR have the body's pattern in their top half and foam boiling out of the pool in the rest, a different set of blobs in each frame, held for 3 ticks each, the body's time, so the streaks above the foam keep sliding at one speed. Beside it, pool.0 and pool.1 are plain still water, and the cliff's rock is rock.0 to rock.2 and its edges.

pages.head: Level 3: The Fire on the Hill
pages.html:
Level 3: The Fire on the Hill

A hilltop at night with a campfire on it. A BIG FIRE: BIGGER FRAMES, UNEVEN TIMES stands at the start, and SPARKS ARE 3 LOOPS, NEVER SIDE BY SIDE stands past the hill. Walk to the middle and look up: the sparks rise from the fire and fade.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • A big fire is a big picture in loops. Open camp.bbl. The fire is 40 pixels wide and 40 high, so it is four blocks, fire.tl, fire.tr, fire.bl and fire.br (top left and so on), each a loop of four frames with the same times (4, 2, 5 and 3 ticks). They are four rings, but they change on the same ticks, so the four pieces always show the same frame of one picture. Under them are logs.0 and logs.1, and the hill is a dome cut into blocks, hill.00 and so on; the blocks of its plain middle are one block used again.
  • A spark is a dim dot that rises and goes out. spark0, spark1 and spark2 are three loops in which a small ember is low in frame 0, higher in 1 and 2 and gone in frame 3, which lasts much longer (11, 7 and 13 ticks) than the others. A spark spends most of its time dark, so the fire does not look as if it is throwing stones. They are laid in a scatter above the fire, and no two of the same loop are side by side, so the sparks rise at different moments from the fire's flame.
  • The night. The palette's sky ramp is dark blue and the grass and dirt are darker (night.pal). The hall has its own palette too (hall.pal, a dim wall and darker bricks), and the cliff uses the day's (day.pal). Each level lists its own palette file, and the blocks in it use the same color numbers, so one set of art can change its mood.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot give each cell its own clock. The clock belongs to the block number, so every cell of one block changes in the same tick. Two torches that should differ need two blocks, which is why the hall has flameA and flameB.
  • It cannot make a pattern slide smoothly. A block only turns into another block, so the fall moves in jumps of 5 pixels, 6 times a second. That is why its streaks are thin and the pattern repeats every block: a bigger jump would show.
  • It has no random. The flicker is not random. It is a loop of four frames with uneven times, repeating from the first tick. It looks random because the times are not alike.
  • It cannot draw smoke or a glow on the hero. The fire does not light Lami or the hill. Light is only the colors you draw.
  • Every loop costs blocks. Each frame is a block of your 150: a flame of four frames costs four, the fall's body, lip and splash are four columns of four frames each (48 in all), and a fire two blocks across and two high costs 16. Level 2 uses about 115 of the 150.
  • Every loop starts together. When a level begins, every loop is at its first frame, so the first moments of a torch hall or a fire look more alike than later ones.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In hall.bbl, set all four Time values of flameA to 4 and watch a torch go from a flicker to a pulse.
  • Change the Time of flagA.0 and flagB.0 to 12 for a slow flag. Change only one of them and watch the wave break at the join.
  • In falls.bbl, change the Time of every fallM frame from 3 to 6 and watch a slower fall; change only one column and see it step out of line.
  • Draw a candle: a flame of two frames with times of 7 and 3.
  • Draw a flame that turns green on one frame, and a firefly: a spark that does not rest.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
